To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the prey capture behavior of weakly electric fish is likely to involve contributions from multiple sensory modalities, (2) the relative contribution of each modality may change during the course of the behavior, (3) the relative contribution may change as a result of environmental conditions, and (4) the relative contribution is likely to be modality-specific.

the prey detection and localization by weakly electric fish is likely to rely, to different degrees, on three octavolaterals sensory systems: the high- and low-frequency electric sense and the mechanosensory lateral line system.

the development of an integrated model of electrosensitory and mechanosensitory information processing in a weakly electric fish.
the sensory and neural mechanisms underlying the ability of weakly electric fish to capture prey in the absence of visual information.
how sensory information is used in the behavior of a fish that feeds in the absence of visual and chemical cues.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrosensory system is most sensitive to prey in the vicinity of the head, whereas the mechanosensory lateral line is most sensitive to tail motion.
the prey capture event of the weakly electric fish, A. albifrons, is a complex sensory integration problem, which is likely to involve contributions from all three octavolateralis modalities.

the electrosense, mechanosense, and vision all contribute to prey detection and localization, with the relative contribution of each modality varying with the environmental conditions and the stage of the predatory behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sensory modalities used by A. albifrons during prey capture behavior are likely to be complementary, and that a combination of modeling and experimental approaches can help us better understand the relative contributions from each of these modalites.

the prey strike trajectory can be reconstructed from the sensory images, which suggests that the sensory system is capable of generating a spatial representation of the prey that can be used to guide the strike.
the sensory modalities that are most relevant to the behavior are not necessarily those that have been studied the most extensively in the laboratory.
